items.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022
items.q: the last recording I was on, it was a trio recording with a drummer Harvey Sorgen

ctx.x: Yeah it’s always tricky if you have the whole band listening to playbacks. Like everybody wants their fader — let me push that up a little bit.

Well the last recording I was on, it was a trio recording with a drummer Harvey Sorgen and a bass player Joe Fonda. Harvey lives up here but he’s also on the international circuit, and Joe Fonda played with Braxton for about eleven years or so after I had played with Braxton. And we went into a studio up here and recorded some stuff and when we listened back to it I could barely hear the drums. And so I kept asking them to bring more drums, more drums, more drums. And I could see Harvey was like grinning like you…

Yes, it’s usually the other way around. You’ve had, been a recipient of a number of grants over the years. An acquaintance of mine said something once that sounded true but I’m not sure and that was organizations don’t give out grants for arts that aren’t cutting edge. You’re not going to get a grant to compose music like Mozart or to play more bebop. Do you think that’s true?
